title: Contest strategy & speed-solving meta
relevance: Timed OAs are the same game as Div2: rank easy work first, ship correct code fast, and do not bleed attempts; CF/AtCoder rating is almost entirely this meta plus upsolving.
company_notes: Timed OAs (HackerRank/HackerEarth 60–90 min, 2–4 tasks) mirror Div2 ranking—clear implementation/greedy first, leave the trick task last; campus finish-as-many-as-you-can assessments use ICPC-style ranking; take-homes reuse near-miss upsolves as follow-ups; live screens map stuck-timers and edge checks directly.

phases.goal: Candidate recognizes contest meta under time pressure, score/penalty rules, and constraint-driven tagging rather than letter order.

must_hit.point: Contest skill is the loop skim → rank → solve → verify → submit → (later) upsolve under a clock and wrong-attempt tax.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the skim-rank-solve-verify-submit-upsolve loop and mentions time pressure or wrong-attempt cost.

must_hit.point: Open by tagging each problem as speed-impl / observation / known template / skip from statements and constraints—not because it is letter A.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says do not dig into #1 only for being A; tags by type from skim of statements+constraints.

must_hit.point: Constraint bands map algorithm class: n≤20 brute/subsets, n≤400 O(n²)/O(n³), n≤2e5 O(n log n); letter order is a hint, constraints are the truth.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes those constraint cutoffs and says constraints beat letter ranking.

must_hit.point: Scoring meta differs: CF score decay favors early easy solves; ICPC/CF ICPC-mode maximizes solves first then minimizes penalty (time + 10×WA on solved only—unsolved WA is free).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts score decay vs maximize-solves, and states the time + 10×WA / unsolved-WA-free rule.

probes: How do you decide what to open first in a timed Div2 or OA when A looks hard and D has more solves?
What do CF score decay vs ICPC-style ranking change about your first 20 minutes?

hints.1: Think about what the clock and the penalty system are actually taxing.
hints.2: Separate recognition into: skim tags, constraint→algo mapping, and scoring-rule implications.
hints.3: Skim → tag speed/observation/template/skip; use n≤20 / n≤400 / n≤2e5 bands; CF early easy vs ICPC more ACs then time+10×WA on solved only.

phases.goal: Candidate lays out a ranked workflow with skim budget, clear-easy-first order, stuck cut-timers, and a 24h upsolve rule.

must_hit.point: Spend the first ~5–8 min (or about 2–4 min in the compressed workflow) skimming all statements+constraints and ranking before deep thinking on any one problem.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives a skim-all-first budget in the ~5–8 or 2–4 min range and ranks before digging.

must_hit.point: Clear A–B (and easy C) / aim A+B or ABC A–C in ~20–25 min with clean first AC before spending deep time on harder tasks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says bank easy points early; cites ~20–25 min speed band for A+B or ABC A–C.

must_hit.point: Stuck timers: ~5–8 min on A/B with no plan → reread (likely misread); ~12–15 min on C with no plan → park, open D/E, return later.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States both cut-timers and the park-and-read-elsewhere move.

must_hit.point: Within 24h upsolve the easiest unsolved with a real solo attempt, then editorial + re-implement from scratch; virtual missed rated rounds.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions 24h, easiest unsolved, attempt-before-editorial, re-implement, virtuals.

probes: Walk me through your first 25 minutes of a CF Div2 or a 60–90 min OA with 2–4 tasks.
When do you abandon a C and open D, and what do you do after the contest?

hints.1: Start from the open routine, not from coding problem A.
hints.2: Include skim budget, easy-first clear, hard cut-timers, then post-contest upsolve.
hints.3: ~5–8 min skim/tag; A+B in ~20–25 min; ~5–8 / ~12–15 stuck cuts; 24h easiest-unsolved then editorial+reimplement.

phases.goal: Candidate describes pre-submit verification and multi-test hygiene that prevents avoidable WA under a penalty tax.

must_hit.point: Before every submit: re-trace samples by hand and check n=1 / empty / all-equal / MAX (and local-check samples + n=1 / empty / max).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists sample re-trace plus edge cases like n=1, empty, all-equal, MAX.

must_hit.point: Reset all multi-test state between cases—one avoided WA beats 5 minutes of clever coding.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out clearing arrays/flags/sums between tests as penalty hygiene.

must_hit.point: When tagged as DP under pressure, code the tiny transition (e.g. 2-state who-kills-next) rather than redesigning mid-contest.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says ship the small tagged DP transition instead of re-architecting live.

must_hit.point: For constraint-ranked brutes like n≤10, implement try-all 2ⁿ rather than hunting a cleverer approach in-contest.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses n≤10 ⇒ enumerate subsets/masks as the intended speed path.

probes: What do you run locally in the last minute before submitting a multi-test greedy?
How does your submit checklist change when wrong attempts lock or burn score?

hints.1: Focus on verification habits, not the algorithm itself.
hints.2: Samples by hand, extreme n, and multi-test reset are the three pillars.
hints.3: Re-trace samples; check n=1/empty/all-equal/MAX; wipe all multi-test state every case.

phases.goal: Candidate ties time budget and constraint size to which approach is contest-viable.

must_hit.point: Use constraints to pick complexity class in-contest: n≤20 brute/subsets, n≤400 O(n²)/O(n³), n≤2e5 O(n log n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Recites those three bands and picks algo class from n.

must_hit.point: Pattern-tag drills should fire fast once seen—e.g. classic BS-on-answer coded in ≤15 min, or Chat Ban-style monotonic BS in <5 min.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives short coding-fire times for known templates under the clock.

must_hit.point: Observation that kills code beats starting O(n²) when a short check (too many ±, residue, a[1]<a[n]) fits—think briefly before heavy code.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says think a few minutes / prefer observation over jumping to O(n²) or heavy DS.

probes: Given only n and time left, how do you choose between brute, O(n²), and O(n log n)?
When is spending three minutes on an observation cheaper than coding?

hints.1: Answer in terms of n cutoffs and template fire-time, not Big-O trivia.
hints.2: Map n≤20 / n≤400 / n≤2e5, then when observation short-circuits code.
hints.3: Those three constraint bands; BS templates in ≤15 or <5 min once recognized; don’t start O(n²) if a short observation fits.

phases.goal: Candidate names common contest failure modes: misreads, overthink, wrong ranking, and pretest-only ACs.

must_hit.point: Anti-overthink: if a short observation (parity, a[1]<a[n], residue, too many ±) fits samples, code it—do not invent heavy DS on 1400s.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives examples like Element Extermination YES iff a[1]<a[n]; inventing stack/segtree fails the meta.

must_hit.point: Careful statement read: misread of 0/1-type reachability (Trouble Sort) is a free WA and pure penalty bleed.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says WA from misreading conditions, not from hard algorithms.

must_hit.point: Pretest/order traps (e.g. AB-then-BA and BA-then-AB non-overlap): one sample can pass while systest fails.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions checking both orders / non-overlap; classic pretest-pass systest-fail lesson.

must_hit.point: Mis-ranking: starting digit-DP on a residue-trick math problem, or rush-submit without verifying both parts of a block-then-BFS construction, burns attempts.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names wrong-tool ranking or verifying only one half before submit.

probes: What contest mistakes cost you a WA that a 30-second re-read would have prevented?
When have you over-engineered a 1400 and how should you have tagged it instead?

hints.1: Think misread, overthink, and submit-too-soon—not obscure algorithms.
hints.2: Cover observation-vs-heavy-DS, statement traps, and pretest/order failures.
hints.3: Code short observations on 1400s; reread 0/1 conditions; check both AB/BA orders; don’t digit-DP a residue trick or half-verify block+BFS.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Enumerate candidate splits/patterns or ship a known template under the clock; hunting a clever closed form loses rank when speed beats elegance on B/C.
In ICPC-style / campus finish-as-many ranking, one more AC always beats polishing penalty on an already-solved easy; unsolved WA is free, so optimize time+10×WA only on problems you will solve.

tradeoffs.topic: Implementation/greedy first vs trick task last
tradeoffs.strong_answer: In timed OAs and Div2, clear speed-impl/greedy tasks first and leave the observation/trick task for last—wrong attempts can lock or burn score on some platforms.
If samples fit a short observation (too many ± → NO, residue trick, a[1]<a[n]), code that; starting O(n²) or digit-DP is a mis-rank that invites TLE and time bleed.

tradeoffs.topic: In-contest C1 vs hard twin C2
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Bank the easy version’s points and idea in-contest; finish the hard twin (priority queue undo, point updates, stack construction) in the 24h upsolve after a real solo attempt.

gotchas.trap: Digging into letter A first because it is A, while D is the easy solve.
gotchas.correction: Skim all statements+constraints first; rank by speed/observation/template/skip and by solve counts—constraints and ranking beat letter order.

gotchas.trap: Submitting after one sample passes without edge or multi-test checks.
gotchas.correction: Re-trace samples by hand, test n=1/empty/all-equal/MAX, and reset all multi-test state; one avoided WA beats five minutes of clever coding.

gotchas.trap: Inventing stack/segment tree or digit-DP on a short-observation 1400.
gotchas.correction: If parity, a[1]<a[n], residue, or too-many-± fits, code the observation; heavy DS or digit-DP means you mis-ranked the problem.

gotchas.trap: Staying on a C with no plan past ~12–15 min (or A/B past ~5–8 min).
gotchas.correction: Reread A/B on early stuck (likely misread); park C, open D/E, return later—ranking drill over sunk-cost coding.

gotchas.trap: Treating all WA like CF score decay when in ICPC-mode.
gotchas.correction: ICPC-style: maximize solves first; penalty is time + 10×WA on solved only—unsolved WA is free, so don’t polish an easy while a solvable harder task sits open.

gotchas.trap: Rush-submitting a two-part construction (block then BFS) after verifying only one part.
gotchas.correction: Verify both parts before submit—block G-adjacent and path check—or you farm WA under the attempt tax.
